what: A LOCAL CPU run, not the plan's T3.7/T3.8 GPU measurement. Reported because the mechanism it exposes is backend-independent and it changes what the Kaggle run should expect to find.

config.reference_leg: --decode-mode off (one batch per document, 12 forward passes)
candidate_legs: --decode-mode full (2488 forward passes, one token each)

findings: The effect is confined to BATCH SIZE 1. Rows inside the tail leg's 100-token prefill span agree with the 208-token prefill reference at exactly 1.000000 across all 1200 of them. So re-batching at a different size reproduces the reference exactly; only single-token steps diverge.

Disagreement rises monotonically with depth: layer 0 at 0.9979, layer 15 at 0.9763, Spearman +0.96. Consistent with error accumulating through the stack below the router rather than with a per-layer bug.

The two candidate legs measure the same phenomenon. tail scores higher than full only because 1200 of its 2488 rows are prefill rows that agree perfectly; its decoded rows sit at 0.9862, matching full's 0.9857.
logits.bin differs too, so this is arithmetic upstream of the argsort, not a tie-breaking artifact in the top-k itself.
caveats: CPU, not GPU. ggml selects different matmul paths for n=1 (vec-dot against the quantized weight) and n>1 (activation repacking plus GEMM); CUDA has the same split between dequant-mul-mat-vec and mul_mat_q/cuBLAS. The mechanism is present on both backends, but the magnitude on 2x T4 with -ngl 99 is unmeasured and could differ in either direction.
Q4_K_M, not F16. Quantized weights make the n=1 vs n>1 kernel difference larger than it would be at F16.
One model, 2488 tokens. The panel scope decision is whole-panel, so this is the first of seven.
implication: Plan section 0b asserts that teacher-forced prefill yields identical routing to decode, and the whole study interprets prefill measurements as claims about decode-time prefetching. On this configuration that assertion is false by ~1.4% of (token, layer) cells, concentrated in the deep layers the depth analysis reads. If the Kaggle GPU run reproduces it, the framing has to change: the results describe prefill routing, and their decode-time relevance becomes a measured approximation rather than an identity.
